svg.text: Redox: electron transfer, oxidation numbers, disproportionation and agents
Oxidation = loss of electrons, reduction = gain (10.1)

g.text: Fe2+ gives Fe3+ + e-
Zn gives Zn2+ + 2e-
Cl2 + 2e- gives 2Cl-
Cu2+ + 2e- gives Cu
red: Fe2+ and Zn lose electrons and are oxidised
blue: Cl2 and Cu2+ gain electrons and are reduced
oxidation and reduction always occur together: a redox reaction
(photosynthesis and respiration are both redox reactions)
1. uncombined element: 0 (S8, H2, Cl2, Na, Mg, Zn)
2. the more electronegative element is negative (HF: F is -1)
3. group 1 +1, group 2 +2, halogens in binary compounds -1,
H +1 (metal hydrides -1), O -2 (peroxides -1, F2O +2)
4. monatomic ion: equal to its charge (Cl- is -1, Al3+ is +3)
5. sum in a compound = 0; 6. sum in an ion = the ion's charge
O is -2, -1 and -1/2 in H2O, Na2O2 and KO2
S = +4 (Sample 10.1)
S = +6 (Sample 10.2)
Mn = +7 (Sample 10.3)

svg.text: metal with non-metal: metal positive; two non-metals: the more electronegative is negative
Disproportionation (10.3): one element both oxidised and reduced

g.text: 2H2O2 gives 2H2O + O2
Cl2 + 6NaOH gives 5NaCl + NaClO3 + 3H2O
O: -1 to -2 in H2O (reduced) and -1 to 0 in O2 (oxidised)
Cl: 0 to -1 in NaCl (reduced) and 0 to +5 in NaClO3 (oxidised)
possible where an element can exist in several oxidation states

svg.text: Oxidising and reducing agents (10.4) and balancing by oxidation number (10.5)

g.text: oxidising agent: oxidises another substance and is itself reduced (gains e-, oxidation number falls): X + e- gives X-, e.g. Cl + e- gives Cl-
reducing agent: reduces another substance and is itself oxidised (loses e-, oxidation number rises): M gives M+ + e-, e.g. Na gives Na+ + e-

svg.text: Cr falls from +6 to +3 (6 electrons gained per K2Cr2O7); Cl rises from -1 to 0 (2 electrons lost per Cl2), so 3Cl2; the rest balanced by inspection
